propositions: Duplicate CAS push/retry/merge logic across workflows was consolidated into a single Python core module (src/rebar/_store/push.py) that owns all delivery mechanics including five-cycle retry budget, fetch-and-merge recovery, and final-push semantics.

The strict push entrypoint raises typed PushDeliveryError on exhausted delivery; the private Python adapter converts core failures to stderr and nonzero status while preserving reusability for library callers.

Workflows (reconcile-bridge and reconcile-bridge-canary) now contain orchestration only and delegate delivery once through the locked commit-and-push or strict push adapter instead of embedding fetch/merge/retry loops.
Legacy callers (library, CLI, MCP, importer, ticket-store) retain best-effort defaults with keyword-only strict=False flag; no interface breakage or schema change occurred.
All three child stories delivered merged evidence: strict semantics (a8e0f67c8), locked commit-and-push (1532700efd), and workflow cutovers (11a026540b, 039fe7bbde, 511c339a63).
